first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A well-researched guide to getting married in Portugal: regions, palaces, legal steps by passport. There is a line saying a 'Wedded Advisor' plans with you 'from the first enquiry to the last dance', but I honestly can't tell from the top of the page whether Wedded Wonderland is a full service planner, a venue marketplace or a travel site. Nothing up there says who they are or why I'd hire them over the three planners I have open in other tabs.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: The headline is lovely, but the intro reads like four separate facts from a guidebook. 'Speak with a Wedded Advisor' doesn't tell me who that person is or how senior they are. I kept reading because 'Sintra Palace' is the sort of thing we're after, not because I trusted the firm.

attention_map.quote: We confirm dates and venues with you.
attention_map.why: Asking me for my guest count before you've shown me any of your work is too early.

attention_map.quote: Legal and travel details from official sources, including IRN, GOV.UK and Smartraveller.
attention_map.why: Fine for credibility on facts. I had to look up Smartraveller, and it's Australian, so this already feels written for someone else.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.quote: Monserrate's lawns and arches, Sintra. Palace roof works run until the first quarter of 2027.
attention_map.why: This is the most useful part. Real venue names and a practical warning about the roof works. But every image is a grey box, so on this screen I'm judging palaces I can't see.
Good that every region names an airport, which is the first thing our guests will ask. It never says how long the drive is though, apart from Lisbon later on.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra; nothing may be fixed to the heritage. We check the terms with you before you book.
attention_map.why: This is the first time it feels like someone who has actually done this. I'd want to know that.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: It just repeats what I read two sections up. The 'Visa-Free for US, UK and AU Passports' card is handy for our guests.

attention_map.section: Pick the Setting for Your Ceremony
attention_map.quote: We sort Portugal wedding venues into six settings.
attention_map.why: More of the same categories, and still no real venue or real couple.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: Buy-out or venue fee: a buy-out is often charged separately from the venue fee.
attention_map.why: Useful, and senior-sounding. But it covers venue pricing, not what YOU charge me, which is the question I actually have.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Getting There
attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide; we confirm the transfer time for each venue.
attention_map.why: Closest the page gets to 'within two hours of an airport'. It only covers Lisbon, and it's minutes from the city centre, not from the airport.

attention_map.section: Entry rules and Marrying Legally, by Passport
attention_map.quote: The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI, because no US authority exists to issue one.
attention_map.why: Thorough, and good that the US and UK get their own paragraphs. But it's a wall of admin, and the Australian paragraph is the longest. I'd expect my planner to handle this, not hand me a reading list.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: That's a non-answer. No range, no currency, nothing on how your fee works. Every other planner tab I have open at least tells me whether it's a flat fee or a percentage.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan. ... An on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: This is where I expected to see end to end. I get a list of events in a weekend, and 'an on-the-day coordinator' makes it sound like day-of coordination, not full service. Who does design, suppliers, guest logistics, budget?

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Build a guest website in Wonderland Studio ... Start for free
attention_map.why: A free DIY tool is a mixed signal. If I'm paying for full service, why am I building my own guest website?

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Milestone Birthday. Gather family at a wine quinta for a long lunch among the terraces.
attention_map.why: Not relevant to me, and it makes the firm feel like a general events or travel site rather than a specialist destination wedding planner.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Your advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue.
attention_map.why: This is where I needed a name, a face, years of experience and weddings they've done. Instead it's an unnamed 'advisor' and a placeholder image. 'Wedded Privileges ... your advisor explains what the programme offers' tells me nothing.
No idea when, or who. We expect quick replies from someone senior. The form itself is reasonable and asks for budget in free text.

attention_map.quote: 4. How Much Is an Average Wedding in Portugal? There is no single average
attention_map.why: Same dodge on cost again. Most of these answers repeat the sections above.

attention_map.section: Read More About Weddings in Portugal / Trending row
attention_map.quote: Trending row ... Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: 'Trending row' looks like a leftover label. Celebrity wedding gossip links next to where I hoped to find your own real weddings feels cheap, and it reads like you're borrowing other people's weddings because you don't have your own.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: 'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance' and 'Together you shortlist venues and plan the weekend around your guests', plus the weekend list ending in 'An on-the-day coordinator'. No scope of services: design, supplier booking, guest travel, budget management are not mentioned.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: The page never says where the firm is or why it's good at Europe. The only clues are Australian ones (Smartraveller, the longest passport section being Australian), which raise the question without answering it.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Every region names its airport (LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC). Only 'Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre' gives a time, and not from the airport. Nothing for the Douro, Algarve or Comporta.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: 'What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things' and 'We talk you through the options'. The venue contract checklist covers venue pricing quirks and VAT, but nothing about the planner's own fee, and no currency anywhere.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: No real weddings, no couple stories, no testimonials. All images are placeholders labelled as generic scenes. The only weddings linked are celebrity ones ('Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding') and 'A Madeira wedding story' with no indication it's yours.

trust_signals_noticed: Named official sources with links (US Department of State, GOV.UK, Smartraveller, IRN)
'Legal and travel details checked October 2026, with official sources named.'
Specific, insider-sounding venue caveats: Monserrate roof works to Q1 2027, state events can cancel Queluz bookings
Venue contract checklist (exclusivity, buy-out, per day or per guest, VAT)
Separate legal routes for US and UK passports
turn_offs_noticed: Vague scope: 'every weekend is built to your plan' with no list of services
No reply time or seniority on the form: 'A Wedded Advisor will reply.'
Off-topic sections (milestone birthday, proposal) and a free DIY tool dilute the full service feel
Celebrity wedding links under a stray 'Trending row' label

images.status: Every image on the screens is a grey placeholder, so I reacted to labels and captions only.
images.would_stop_me: pena-palace-sintra-hills-wedding-in-portugal.jpg in the hero and monserrate-palace-arches-lawns-sintra.jpg, if they're real and beautiful. Palaces are the hook for us.
felt_generic_or_stock: quinta-stone-staircase-couple-portugal.jpg and lisbon-arrival-couple-city-street.jpg: sounds like an anonymous stock couple
wedded-advisor-planning-with-couple.jpg: if this isn't a real, named planner it does the opposite of what I need
algarve-beach-low-sun.jpg and the many repeated Douro terrace images: same scene three or four times
images.missing: Any photo of a real wedding you planned in Portugal, and a real headshot of the planner.

emotional_response.overall: Impressed by the research, cold on the firm.
emotional_response.detail: I came away knowing more about Portuguese civil registry than I wanted to, and nothing about the people who'd plan our wedding. Nothing here makes me feel anyone would be emotionally invested in us. It reads like a very good encyclopedia entry with a contact form attached.

payload.decision_reason: Fails my threshold on all three counts: no proof of weddings they've done in Portugal, no fee structure or currency, and no named senior planner. 'An on-the-day coordinator' even makes me doubt it's full service. I might come back to the legal section as a reference, but this firm won't make our shortlist against planners who show their work and their fees.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly this is a better Portugal guide than most planners' sites, and the bit about state events cancelling Queluz bookings is exactly the sort of thing I'd want a planner to know. But I'm comparing firms, not reading up on Portugal. Who are you? Who's my planner? Where are the weddings you've done? What do you charge, and in what currency? I scrolled to the form looking for any of that and got 'A Wedded Advisor will reply' and a list of celebrity weddings. Closing the tab.
